item.description:
Tide Launches Raziel AI Security Tool Assuming Breach Imminence

Tide launched Raziel, an AI security tool designed under the assumption that hackers already exist within networks. This release addresses escalating risks from AI-generated code vulnerabilities and advanced attack models.

🔍 Overview

Tide’s Raziel operates on the principle that “hackers are inside”, acknowledging systemic flaws in traditional security paradigms. Co-founder Michael Loewy asserts the industry was losing ground to attackers even before AI, noting:

Before AI, a developer needed to be perfect all the time—perfectly patched, free of errors—while an attacker only needed one mistake to breach. It’s virtually impossible, which is why breaches are daily news. AI exacerbates this by enabling rapid production of error-prone code alongside sophisticated vulnerability exploitation.

🧩 How it works

Raziel implements emergent authority, where access permissions dynamically materialize only when identity, policy, context, and intent align—then dissolve. This replaces static credential storage with cryptographic fragmentation, ensuring no single point of failure exists. As Loewy states:

The problem is authority always lives somewhere, and someone always has access. We distribute it architecturally so nothing is inheritable.

Google Research introduces WikiSkill to give AI agents persistent memory

Google Research has introduced a framework called WikiSkill, which separates an AI model’s core intelligence from its procedural memory. By allowing agents to record and learn from their past performance, the system enables models to improve task execution without requiring fine-tuning or changes to the model’s parametric memory.

🧩 How it works

The WikiSkill system functions through three distinct layers:

  • Raw layer: Silently records detailed execution traces of tasks, including API calls, searched websites, and success or failure data.
  • Wiki layer: Utilizes a ‘Wiki Maintainer’ to analyze raw logs and distill them into generalized lessons stored in a structured wiki.
  • Skill proposer: Translates wiki insights into targeted procedural instructions, known as skills, which are provided to the agent only when relevant.

⚙️ Key details

The system employs a gating mechanism to maintain performance quality. Before a new skill is implemented, it is tested against a validation dataset. If performance decreases compared to the baseline, the skill is rejected and rolled back.

🚀 Inside Google’s Open-Source Gemini Research Agent: Building AI That Actually Does The Deep Work

Summary: Google has open-sourced a powerful AI research assistant built with Gemini 2.5 and LangGraph that goes beyond simple answers to perform iterative, citation-backed research. This blog explores how this full-stack solution dynamically generates queries, evaluates information gaps, and refines its approach—offering developers a blueprint for creating sophisticated AI research tools.

🧠 The Evolution of AI Research Assistants

The promise of AI has always included automating tedious research tasks, but most solutions have fallen short—offering quick answers without the depth, transparency, or reliability needed for serious work. Google’s latest open-source project significantly changes this landscape.

The “Gemini Fullstack LangGraph Quickstart” represents a substantial leap forward in AI research capabilities. Unlike simple chatbots, this system doesn’t just respond to queries—it actively investigates them through a sophisticated, multi-stage process that mirrors human research workflows.

What makes this project particularly valuable is its transparent architecture, combining Google’s powerful Gemini models with the flexibility of the open-source LangGraph framework. The result? A research agent that not only finds information but evaluates it, identifies knowledge gaps, and iteratively refines its approach until it can deliver a comprehensive, citation-backed response.

🔍 Breaking Down the Architecture: How It Actually Works

The project is structured as a full-stack application with clear separation between frontend and backend:

1
2

frontend/ - React application built with Vite
backend/ - LangGraph and FastAPI application

But the real magic happens in the LangGraph-powered research agent, which follows a remarkably human-like research process:

  1. 🎯 Generate Initial Queries: The agent first uses Gemini to understand the user’s request and generate relevant search queries.

  2. 🌐 Web Research: For each query, it searches the web using the Google Search API to fetch relevant information.

  3. 🤔 Reflection & Knowledge Gap Analysis: In perhaps its most impressive feature, the agent then analyzes the search results to identify what information is still missing.

  4. 🔄 Iterative Refinement: If knowledge gaps exist, it generates follow-up queries specifically targeting those gaps and repeats the process until satisfied.

  5. 📝 Finalize Answer: The agent synthesizes its findings into a coherent response with citations to original sources.

This cyclical process of querying, researching, reflecting, and refining enables the agent to conduct surprisingly thorough investigations—a far cry from the superficial responses we’ve grown accustomed to from many AI systems.

🛠️ The Technical Stack: How It All Fits Together

The project brings together several specialized technologies:

  • Frontend: React via Vite, with Tailwind CSS and Shadcn UI for styling
  • Backend: LangGraph for agent orchestration, FastAPI for API endpoints
  • Core AI: Google Gemini models power the reasoning, search, and synthesis
  • Production Infrastructure: Redis for pub-sub messaging and PostgreSQL for persistence

𝗟𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗚𝗿𝗮𝗽𝗵 deserves special attention here. This open-source library from LangChain enables developers to define complex workflows as graphs, where nodes represent computations (often LLM calls) and edges represent the flow of state and decisions. It’s specially designed for building stateful, multi-actor applications with LLMs—perfect for the kind of iterative research process this agent performs.

Setting up the project locally requires:

  • Python 3.8+ for the backend
  • Node.js for the frontend
  • A Gemini API key

The project’s GitHub repository (https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-fullstack-langgraph-quickstart) provides detailed setup instructions, including Docker configurations for production deployment.

🔮 Why This Matters: Beyond Simple Q&A

What makes this project significant isn’t just its technical sophistication—it’s how it reimagines what AI research assistants can do. By implementing a reflective, iterative approach, it addresses several critical limitations of traditional Q&A systems:

  • 🧩 Handling Complex Questions: Rather than giving up when a single search doesn’t yield enough information, it identifies knowledge gaps and continues investigating.

  • 📊 Transparency: By providing citations and tracking its research process, it allows users to verify information and understand how conclusions were reached.

  • 🔄 Adaptability: The dynamic query generation and refinement process means it can navigate unfamiliar topics without relying solely on training data.

This represents a fundamentally different approach to AI assistants—one focused on augmenting human research capabilities rather than simply providing quick answers.

🌟 Building Your Own Deep Research AI

Perhaps the most exciting aspect of this project is that it’s open-sourced under the Apache License 2.0. This means developers can:

  • Study the architecture to understand best practices for building sophisticated AI agents
  • Customize and extend the system for specialized research tasks
  • Integrate the approach into their own applications

The combination of Google’s powerful Gemini models with the flexibility of open-source frameworks like LangGraph creates a powerful foundation for building trustworthy, capable AI research tools that go beyond the limitations of simpler systems.

🔭 The Future of AI-Powered Research

As we look ahead, this project offers a glimpse into a future where AI doesn’t just answer questions but becomes a true research partner—one that can discover, evaluate, synthesize, and present information with a level of depth and transparency that builds genuine trust.

The question now isn’t whether AI can help with research—it’s how to best architect these systems to complement human intelligence rather than attempting to replace it. Google’s open-source approach here points to a collaborative future where powerful proprietary models combined with transparent, adaptable frameworks create tools that genuinely augment our cognitive capabilities.

What research problems might you solve with an agent that can investigate topics with thoroughness, transparency, and adaptability? The tools to build such systems are now within reach.

  • New data you create
  • Third-party data

The symposium showcased how Merck Research Labs exemplifies this approach. Their team created a clinical data layer on AWS that consolidates clinical and operational information across studies onto a single platform, enabling automation that dramatically accelerates processes.

Another game-changing element is real-world data (RWD). Consider this striking statistic: 85% of FDA drug approvals between 2019-2021 leveraged real-world evidence. Despite its proven value, working with RWD has historically been slow and frustrating—taking up to four months to process. AWS partnerships have reduced this timeline to as little as two weeks.

📸 Imagine a data pipeline visualization showing the transformation from months-long processes to weeks

The collaboration between AWS, the Broad Institute, and Manifold AI further illustrates this data revolution. This partnership combines seamless data access with advanced analysis capabilities using AWS HealthOmics, Amazon Bedrock, and Anthropic’s Claude to power AI-driven research at unprecedented scales.

🤖 From Experiments to Excellence: Scaling What Works

A clear trend emerged from the symposium: forward-thinking organizations have moved beyond random AI experiments to strategically scaling successful use cases.

Johnson & Johnson’s approach exemplifies this shift. The company has pivoted to focus exclusively on their highest-value AI applications—a strategy that enables faster ROI, better resource allocation, and sustainable innovation.

Sanofi provided another compelling case study. Their AI-powered assistant “Concierge” delivers contextual answers about company policies and procedures. The impressive adoption rate—over 80% of Sanofi employees—demonstrates how deeply AI can integrate when it solves genuine daily challenges.

The most successful implementations target specific high-impact challenges. Working with PwC, AWS identified several use cases delivering significant value:

  • 🔍 Biomarker Discovery: AI agents mining literature and first-party data
  • 📋 Regulatory Amendment Analysis: Reducing costly protocol amendments through AI-powered feedback analysis
  • 🧪 Clinical Trial Analysis: AI-guided exploration accelerating insights
  • 🏭 Manufacturing Execution System Chat: Natural language interfaces extracting actionable intelligence
  • 💼 Sales Concierge: Supporting commercial teams with timely, relevant data
  • 🔐 Fraud Detection: AI-driven anomaly detection in drug pricing programs
  • 📈 Protocol Generation: Accelerating clinical trial design through AI-assisted drafting

To facilitate adoption, AWS has created the Life Sciences Generative AI Portal—a curated collection of over 40 generative AI demos and customizable prototypes already delivering value across R&D, clinical development, manufacturing, and commercial operations.

🧠 The Next Frontier: Agentic AI in Action

Perhaps the most exciting developments centered around 𝙖𝙜𝙚𝙣𝙩𝙞𝙘 𝘼𝙄—AI systems that can independently perform complex sequences of tasks to achieve specific goals.

Genentech showcased this potential with a striking example: A distinguished scientist completed a complex analysis of cell surface receptors in just 10 minutes using agentic AI—a task that previously required two full days of work.

To accelerate adoption across the industry, AWS recently introduced an open-source agentic AI toolkit built on Amazon Bedrock. This toolkit includes:

  • Research Agents: For target identification, biomarker discovery, and experimental design
  • Clinical Agents: Supporting trial analysis, protocol optimization, and patient stratification
  • Commercial Agents: Generating competitive intelligence and market insights

📸 Conceptual illustration of multiple AI agents working together to solve complex research problems

Publisher Wiley collaborated on an agent capable of searching full-text articles published under creative commons licenses. This agent delivers reliable, cited insights in minutes rather than the hours or days typically required for literature review—a transformational time-saving tool for researchers.

The toolkit’s architecture allows individual agents to connect with multi-agent supervisors using Amazon Bedrock’s collaboration capabilities, enabling developers to orchestrate across agents and build sophisticated workflows.

🚀 Building on a Foundation for Future Innovation

The symposium made clear that while technology continues advancing at breakneck speed, success depends on establishing a scalable, secure data foundation. This foundation enables organizations to adapt and evolve regardless of what innovations emerge next.

The life sciences industry stands at an inflection point where AI is transitioning from experimental to essential. Organizations that unify their data, implement strategic AI use cases, and embrace agentic capabilities are positioned to lead the next wave of healthcare breakthroughs.

What will your organization’s AI strategy prioritize in this rapidly evolving landscape? Will you focus on data integration, specific use case implementation, or exploring agentic capabilities?

🤖 Democratizing Data Science: How Amazon Q Developer is Revolutionizing Machine Learning for Everyone

𝙎𝙪𝙢𝙢𝙖𝙧𝙮: Amazon Q Developer in SageMaker Canvas transforms ML model creation from a weeks-long expert task into a natural language conversation. This AI agent system lets non-technical users build sophisticated machine learning models in minutes through simple dialogue, automatically handling data preparation, model selection, and optimization while providing transparency into the entire process.

🚀 The Machine Learning Revolution Just Got More Accessible

Machine learning has traditionally stood behind a wall of technical expertise. Building predictive models typically requires specialized knowledge in data science, machine learning algorithms, and a thorough understanding of business contexts. Even for experts, the process from data acquisition to model deployment can stretch across days or weeks.

But what if you could simply ask for the machine learning model you need?

That’s exactly what Amazon Q Developer in SageMaker Canvas delivers. Generally available since February 28, 2025 (after its beta preview at re:Invent 2024), this generative-AI-powered assistant lets anyone build and deploy sophisticated machine learning models through natural language conversation—no ML expertise required.

📸 See illustration above showing the chatbot interface of Amazon Q Developer for SageMaker Canvas

🧠 How Amazon Q Developer Works: AI Agency in Action

At its core, Amazon Q Developer functions as an 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝘀𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺—an autonomous AI that acts on your behalf. Here’s the fascinating part: the system combines a large language model (LLM) interface with a structured nonvolatile-memory block that retains critical information throughout your conversation.

The workflow begins with you describing your business problem in plain language. For example, you might say: “I’m a credit risk analyst at a bank and want to classify loan applicants as default or non-default based on their financial characteristics and economic indicators.”

From there, you can:

  • Select an existing dataset
  • Create a new dataset from S3, Redshift, SQL, or Snowflake
  • Simply upload a CSV file from your computer

The system expects tabular data with target columns (what you want to predict) and feature columns (data points used for prediction). For time-series forecasting, you’ll also need a timestamp column.

📸 See illustration showing the architecture of Q Developer data science assistant

What makes this system truly powerful is its dependency graph structure—each node represents a problem variable like problem_type, evaluation_metric, or target_column. This architecture helps the agent infer missing variables necessary for building your ML model.

🔍 Automatic Intelligence: From Data to Predictions

Once you’ve provided your dataset and described your problem, Amazon Q Developer takes over with remarkable autonomy:

🧹 Intelligent Data Preparation

The system automatically:

  • Cleans data and fills missing values
  • Encodes categorical features
  • Handles outliers
  • Removes duplicate rows/columns

Throughout this process, you can ask follow-up questions about your dataset (e.g., “What percentage of rows have missing values?” or “Are there outliers?”) and use DataWrangler for advanced analytics and visualization.

🤖 Sophisticated Model Building

Amazon Q Developer doesn’t just build a single machine learning model—it creates an 𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗹𝗲 of models including XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, linear models, and neural networks.

The system automatically:

  • Identifies the appropriate ML task type (classification, regression, or forecasting)
  • Suggests appropriate loss functions based on your needs
  • Conducts hyperparameter optimization (HPO)
  • Manages feature engineering

All of these complex processes are handled behind the scenes, without requiring any technical input from you.

📸 See illustration showing dataset analysis with Q Developer in SageMaker Canvas

📊 Transparent Results and Deployment

After training, you can:

  • Run inference on test datasets
  • Deploy your model as a SageMaker inference endpoint in just a few clicks
  • Access an automatically generated explainability report

The explainability report is particularly valuable, offering visualizations and insights into:

  • Dataset properties
  • Feature attribution scores (which variables matter most)
  • The model training process
  • Performance metrics

💡 Why This Matters: The Democratization of ML

The significance of Amazon Q Developer extends far beyond convenience. This tool represents a fundamental shift in who can access the power of machine learning:

  1. Breaking down technical barriers: Business analysts, domain experts, and other non-technical professionals can now leverage advanced ML without waiting for data science teams.

  2. Accelerating development cycles: What once took weeks can now be accomplished in minutes or hours.

  3. Maintaining quality: By using ensemble methods and automatic optimization, the system often achieves performance comparable to models built by experienced data scientists.

  4. Preserving transparency: Unlike many AI systems, Q Developer provides clear explanations about model decisions and feature importance.

For organizations looking to become more data-driven, this technology offers a path to widespread ML adoption without massive investments in specialized talent or extended development timelines.

🔮 The Future of Human-AI Collaboration in Data Science

Amazon Q Developer represents an early glimpse into a future where AI agents work alongside humans, handling the technical complexities while humans focus on problem definition and business insights.

Rather than replacing data scientists, tools like this expand the ecosystem, allowing experts to focus on more complex challenges while empowering non-specialists to solve predictive problems independently.

As these systems evolve, we can expect even more intuitive interfaces, better automated feature engineering, and deeper integration with business intelligence systems—ultimately making ML as accessible as spreadsheet formulas are today.

Ready to transform your data into powerful ML models without extensive data science expertise? Start exploring Amazon Q Developer in SageMaker Canvas today and experience the simplicity of building ML models using natural-language commands.

What business problem could you solve with a conversational ML assistant at your fingertips? 🤔
